Definition: from a compound of G5259 and a derivative of G3700; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions):--keep under, weary.
BiblicalUsage: hypōpiázō turns up where the Bible says to beat black and blue, to wear out. In Luke 18:5, the text says "lest by her continual coming she weary me."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, hypōpiázō means to beat black and blue, to wear out, and I leave it at that.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
